strengths: Novel theoretical framework extending diffusion wavelets to vector-valued signals with proven SE(3)-equivariance via local SVD-based coordinate systems
Strong theoretical guarantees: frame bounds (Theorem 3.1) and equivariance properties (Theorems 3.2-3.3) with detailed rigorous proofs
Impressive parameter efficiency: achieves comparable performance to EGNN with 59,779 parameters vs. 284,036 (79% reduction) and vs. TFN with 99.8% fewer parameters
Clear demonstration of equivariance importance through test set rotation experiments showing dramatic failure of non-equivariant variants
Avoids oversmoothing problem of message-passing networks through single-layer multiscale feature extraction
Comprehensive technical documentation: detailed proofs, architectural specifications, complexity analysis supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical limitation: experiments exclusively on synthetic data (random ellipsoids with 512 graphs of 128 nodes). No real-world validation on molecular, protein, or other standard benchmarks where geometric equivariance is practically important

Insufficient exploration of design choices: no ablation studies on Gaussian kernel scale ϵ, minimum degree requirement (ni ≥ d), or SVD degeneracy assumptions; robustness of sign-flipping procedure not empirically validated
Frame bounds depend on dmin/dmax singular value ratio with no analysis of performance on irregular graphs where this ratio is unfavorable

Restrictive activation function constraint requiring σ to commute with rotations (Theorem 3.3); while constructible, standard activations (ReLU, tanh) don't satisfy this, limiting practical flexibility
Graph modification requirement: enforcing ni ≥ d by adding edges alters graph structure in ways that could affect structure-sensitive tasks; impact not explored
Limited baseline comparisons: missing recent equivariant methods (NequIP, Allegro, etc.) and other equivariant scattering approaches mentioned in related work

Gap between theory and implementation: method uses non-dyadic InfoGain-selected wavelets, removes nonlinearity from scattering coefficients, adds Dirac features—modifications not formally justified despite claims theoretical guarantees adapt
Incomplete complexity analysis: O(d∑ki²) SVD cost per node could be prohibitive for large-degree nodes; no empirical scaling analysis beyond wall-clock timing

strengths: Rigorous theoretical analysis with proven frame bounds and rotational equivariance properties (Theorems 3.1-3.3)
Significant parameter efficiency gains compared to baselines (20K-60K vs 300K-29M parameters), with practical benefits for deployment
Comprehensive experimental validation across three diverse domains (synthetic, wind, neural data) with proper cross-validation and statistical testing
Well-designed ablation studies clearly demonstrating the importance of equivariance (Table 1 shows dramatic failure of non-equivariant models under rotation)
Natural extension from scalar diffusion wavelets with clear motivation from vector diffusion maps and principled mathematical framework
Excellent presentation with effective visualizations (Figures 3-4) and detailed appendices supporting reproducibility
Automatic translation invariance and thorough computational complexity analysis
weaknesses: Marginal or absent empirical improvements: wind task shows VDW-GNN (2.75 MSE) statistically indistinguishable from EGNN (2.77 MSE), neural task shows no significant difference vs MARBLE (p > 0.05)
Limited novelty: extending scalar to vector wavelets via local SVD-based rotations is straightforward; frame bounds result is expected given orthogonal transformation properties
Unclear practical guidance: paper fails to identify when VDW-GNNs should be preferred over simpler equivariant methods (EGNN, TFN)
Restrictive activation function requirement (Theorem 3.3): activation must commute with rotations, limiting architectural flexibility with suggested radial function solution
Suspicious baseline comparison: DD-TNN performs catastrophically worse (12.76 vs 2.75 MSE) with no explanation, raising questions about fair comparison or setup bias favoring VDW-GNN

Arbitrary graph construction choices: k-NN graphs lack sensitivity analysis; artificial edge addition when deg(vi) < D could affect geometric validity; wind experiment uses artificial directional edges
Primary advantage is parameter efficiency rather than predictive accuracy, providing limited motivation for adoption in modern deep learning where memory is less constrained than accuracy
Incomplete reproducibility: code URL missing; many hyperparameter choices appear ad-hoc; InfoGain wavelets procedure adds undocumented complexity
Limited scope of real-world experiments: small graphs (≤2000 nodes); neural data uses derived velocity features rather than raw signals; scalability to large graphs not addressed
Frame bounds result lacks practical context: connection between tighter bounds and generalization performance is not established; implications for learning unclear
